Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwoodinference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com>

Subject: Recap: Discovery + Proposed POC Scope for ClearSky Health (Search Assistant)

Hi Tom / Sarah —

Thanks again for the conversation this morning. Below is a short recap of what we heard and a proposed, timeboxed POC scope so we can validate impact quickly. Please flag anything I missed or got wrong.

Key pain points you shared
- Clinicians struggle to find relevant patient-guidelines and prior-visit notes quickly; average search time ~3–4 minutes and frequent false positives.
- Current search is keyword-based, brittle to phrasing and synonyms across specialties.
- Compliance requirement: PHI must not leave your VPC; audit trail of model queries required.

Success criteria for POC (agreed signals)
- Precision: reduce false positive rate on target queries by >=40% over baseline (evaluation set we agreed).
- Latency: median search response <=350ms for 256-token queries under sample load.
- Security: all traffic routed to ClearSky VPC, keys managed by your KMS; audit log available.

Proposed 4-week POC scope (goal: validate quality + ops)
Week 0 (this week): access + environment setup — we need S3 read access to the deidentified doc corpus, service account for our engineer, and a short allowlist of sample prompt templates.
Week 1: model integration + prompt set (10–15 canonical prompts covering triage, guideline lookup, notes summarization).
Week 2: evaluation run — run held-out queries, log outputs, and compute precision/recall against your annotator labels.
Week 3: performance tuning — batching, KV cache settings, and latency load tests; wrap up with final report and go/no-go recommendation.

Owners
- Redwood: Rishi (SE) — infra + access, Marissa (CS) — success criteria and evaluation coordination.
- ClearSky: Tom — product lead; Sarah — clinical SME; Procurement (procurement@clearsky.health) — contracting point.

Access checklist (needs from ClearSky)
- Service account (IAM) for Redwood with read access to test S3 bucket or a temporary signed URL set.
- List of 200 representative queries and 100 labeled positives/negatives for eval.
- IP allowlist for load testing (we’ll share IP range).

Attachments: POC SOW (attached), access-checklist.xlsx (attached).

Next steps (proposed immediate actions)
1) Tom/Sarah confirm access items and share timeline for procurement (target: grant test access by Mon 11/23).
2) Rishi to send terraform/kube access instructions and short IAM role template.
3) Naomi to schedule kickoff once access confirmed — I’ll propose Wed/Thu next week.

Thanks — looking forward to getting started.

Best,
Naomi Feldman
Enterprise AE | Redwood Inference
naomi@redwoodinference.com | +1 (415) 555-0123

Naomi — thanks for the thorough recap. Looks good; a few clarifications from our side: 

1) Data access: we can provision a time-limited S3 bucket in our security account (non-prod) and create a read-only role for your service account. IT mentions it will take two business days once procurement signs off.
2) Labels: we can deliver the 100 labeled queries by next Tuesday (11/24). Will Sarah confirm?
3) Compliance: audit logs are mandatory but we prefer no model artifacts to leave our VPC. We discussed a private deployment option; can you include minimal steps and rough ETA for Private deployment in the SOW?

On timelines — procurement may need a short statement of no-PHI exposure and our SOC2 clause. I’m looping procurement on this thread.

Tom

Thanks Naomi / Tom — quick technical notes and what we’ll need to move week 0 quickly:

- Private deployment note: we can run Redwood Private inside your VPC. Typical ETA for a small POC cluster (2 GPUs + control plane) is ~5 business days after network/VPN and KMS access are provided. I’ve added a short checklist in the access-checklist.xlsx (attached) with ports and CIDRs.
- Service account: please provide AWS account ID and exact role name; if you prefer we can produce a CloudFormation template to create the role (faster).
- Sample prompts: we recommend 12 canonical prompts (I’ll paste a starter set in a separate email) that cover: guideline lookup, note extraction, cross-visit summarization, and synonym expansion.
- Eval harness: we’ll run an offline evaluation first (no model calls out of your VPC) using held-out labels, then run a constrained live test to verify latency under simulated load.

I’ll follow up with the CFN and a minimal network diagram. Happy to hop on a short tech call if that helps accelerate approvals.

—Rishi
